run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-15T03:32:59Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for otel-demo/frontend is explained by an outage of its single-replica dependency ad that began immediately after an intentional pod-template restart of the ad Deployment at 2026-11-15T03:31:48Z. Over the alert window 02:32:59Z-03:54:48Z the frontend recorded 1711.8 ERROR span increases against 106117.9 UNSET, and the error spans are confined to one call path: grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds (424.1), its parent executing api route (pages) /api/data (424.1), GET /api/data (424.1), the top-level GET span (424.1), plus tcp.connect (15.2); every other frontend operation recorded zero error spans. On the dependency side the ad service stopped emitting GetAds server spans: 208.9 in the 300s window ending 03:32:59, 0 in the window ending 03:37:59, then 124.3 and 97.5 as it recovered. Frontend GetAds error spans run from the buckets around 03:33 to 03:39-03:41 and are zero from 03:41 onward, and the final 720s of the window show zero frontend ERROR spans. The restart was controller-driven (new ReplicaSet ad-d89765fb5 scaled 0->1, old ad-554b849958 scaled 1->0, old pod ad-554b849958-gcmfq stopped at 03:31:51; template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-15T03:31:48Z). The replacement pod ad-d89765fb5-whfnz was marked Ready at 03:31:51 while its application was not yet serving: its only log line 'Ad service starting.' is stamped 03:36:01, and the ad container has no readiness, liveness or startup probe, so the ad Service put it in rotation before its gRPC port accepted connections. Gaps: Jaeger holds no traces after ~03:29:33, so the exact gRPC error string is unknown and the connection-failure character is inferred from client ERROR/tcp.connect spans plus the ad serving gap; the RequestErrorRate rule itself is absent from this Prometheus, so its expression and the reported 2.3555 value could not be verified.

claims.text: In the alert window the frontend service recorded 1711.8 span increases with status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR and 106117.9 with STATUS_CODE_UNSET (span counts, not request counts).

Frontend error spans are concentrated on exactly these operations and nowhere else in the returned set: GET 424.1, GET /api/data 424.1, executing api route (pages) /api/data 424.1, grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds 424.1 and tcp.connect 15.2, while GET /api/cart, POST, POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout, executing api route /api/cart, executing api route /api/checkout, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder were all 0.

For the frontend's client span grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds the window totals were 424.1 ERROR and 1571.8 UNSET; dns.lookup had 16.2 UNSET and no ERROR, and tcp.connect had 15.2 ERROR against 1.0 UNSET.

The ad service's own GetAds server spans carry no ERROR status in the window: oteldemo.AdService/GetAds 1551.1 with STATUS_CODE_UNSET, getAdsByCategory 1340.2 and getRandomAds 429.8 with STATUS_CODE_UNSET; the only ad ERROR series are flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream (1.02) and ResolveBoolean (0).

Ad service GetAds span counts are 254.4, 242.2, 247.8 and 238.9 for the 300s windows ending 03:12:59 through 03:27:59, 208.9 for the window ending 03:32:59, then 0 for the window ending 03:37:59, then 124.3 (03:42:59) and 97.5 (03:47:59) - i.e. a serving gap covering roughly 03:33-03:41 followed by recovery.

Frontend grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds ERROR spans were 0 in every 60s bucket from 03:29 to 03:32, then non-zero: 38.4 (bucket ending 03:33), 108, 139.2, 139.2, 133.2, 126.6, 129.1, 127.2, 56.4 (ending 03:41), then 0 from 03:42 onward.
Frontend tcp.connect ERROR spans were 0 up to the bucket ending 03:32:59, then 8.4 (03:33:59), 10.8, 4.8, 2.4, 2.4, ~2.39, ~2.31, 2.4 and back to 0 from 03:41 onward.

A 120s-step series of frontend ERROR span increases shows 0 for every bucket from 03:08:59 through the bucket ending 03:31, then 42.67 on GET / GET /api/data / executing api route /api/data / grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds (bucket ending ~03:33), 77.3, 106.0, 78.67, then 0 for the buckets ending 03:41, 03:43 and 03:45.

Kubernetes events in otel-demo show a rollout at 03:31:48-03:31:51: ScalingReplicaSet ad-d89765fb5 from 0 to 1, SuccessfulCreate of pod ad-d89765fb5-whfnz, ScalingReplicaSet ad-554b849958 from 1 to 0, Killing/Stopping container ad on pod ad-554b849958-gcmfq at 03:31:51, and SuccessfulDelete of that pod.
The replacement pod ad-d89765fb5-whfnz was created 03:31:48, its ad container started 03:31:50, and the pod's Ready condition has been True since 03:31:51 with restartCount 0 and empty lastState.

The new ad ReplicaSet's pod template carries the annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-15T03:31:48Z while ad-554b849958 does not, so the new ReplicaSet came from an intentional Deployment restart, not an image change.

Both ad ReplicaSet pod templates are otherwise identical: image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad, the same env (AD_PORT 8080, FLAGD_HOST flagd, FLAGD_PORT 8013, OTEL collector variables), port 8080, and limits cpu 50m / memory 450Mi with requests cpu 10m / memory 225Mi.

The ad and frontend containers define no readinessProbe, livenessProbe or startupProbe (all null), so container start alone marks the pod Ready behind the ad Service (ClusterIP 100.64.219.118, port 8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=ad).

The only log line read from the new ad container is 'Ad service starting.' at 2026-11-15T03:36:01.903Z, about four minutes after the container started at 03:31:50; no previous container instance exists to read.

The failure propagated through the ingress tier: frontend-proxy recorded 424.1 ERROR spans on 'router frontend egress' and 455.6 on 'ingress' over the window, with per-300s values 0, 0, 0 before 03:32, then 35.6 (03:32:59), 248.9 (03:37:59), 72.2 (03:42:59) and 0 (03:47:59) for the egress operation.
The frontend pod was not restarted or replaced during the window: frontend-675fd7b5c5-c8fk6 was created 02:59:21, owned by ReplicaSet frontend-675fd7b5c5, with restartCount 0 and empty lastState.

Recovery is visible in the telemetry: the frontend ERROR-span increase over the final 720s of the window (03:42:48-03:54:48) evaluates to 0, and ad GetAds span counts are back to 124.3 (window ending 03:42:59) and 97.5 (ending 03:47:59).

A pre-incident sampled trace (03:29:28, trace 645c70fab86dff58e7239eb9c67494e2) shows the normal path ad GetAds -> frontend GET /api/data -> GET with rpc.grpc.status_code=0 and http.status_code=200, all with no error rows, so the path was working before the restart.

Primary cause: the intentional ad Deployment restart at 03:31:48 removed the only ad replica; the replacement pod was reported Ready at 03:31:51 although its application was not yet listening (first log line at 03:36:01, zero ad GetAds server spans in the window ending 03:37:59). Because no readiness probe exists, the ad Service routed GetAds traffic to that not-yet-serving pod, so frontend grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds calls failed (ERROR client spans plus tcp.connect errors) until ad began serving again around 03:40-03:42, producing the errors on GET /api/data and its parent GET spans that drove the RequestErrorRate alert.

Contributing factor (not established): the ad container's CPU limit of 50m against a 10m request is very low for a JVM service, which could explain why the restarted ad process needed minutes (first log at 03:36:01) before it accepted connections; no CPU-throttling or JVM startup metric was queried, so this remains unverified.

Rejected: the ad service returned application-level errors for GetAds. The ad service emitted zero GetAds server spans in the window ending 03:37:59 (so requests never reached a working handler), and no ad ERROR status was recorded on GetAds, getAdsByCategory or getRandomAds in the window.

Rejected: the frontend itself was broken or restarted. Its pod dates from 02:59:21 with restartCount 0 and empty lastState, and its error spans are confined to the AdService/GetAds path while cart, checkout, product-catalog and recommendation operations recorded zero error spans.

Rejected as this cause: the flagd error spans on ad (1.02), fraud-detection (2.04) and recommendation (4.06) over the whole window are scattered singleton EventStream/Resolve events appearing in buckets before, during and after the incident (ad 1.11 at 03:27:59, 0 at 03:32:59 and 03:37:59; recommendation 1.11 at 03:12:59 and 03:22:59), with ResolveBoolean/ResolveInt errors at 0, and are not concentrated in the GetAds failure interval.

Add a readinessProbe (and a startupProbe) on the ad container's port 8080 so the pod is not marked Ready, and not placed behind the ad Service, until the gRPC server accepts connections; consider raising the 50m CPU limit that throttles JVM startup.

Run the ad Deployment with more than one replica and a PodDisruptionBudget so a rollout restart does not remove the only serving instance; the Deployment's rollingUpdate maxUnavailable is 25% of 1 replica, and the old pod was killed at 03:31:51 before the replacement was functional.

gaps: Jaeger returned no data for frontend traces in 03:30-03:54:48 nor for tags error=true, rpc.grpc.status_code="14" or http.status_code="500" (views with status no_data), and the newest sampled traces end ~03:29:33, so the exact gRPC error code/message of the 424.1 failing GetAds client spans is unknown; the connection-failure character is inferred from tcp.connect ERROR spans plus the ad serving gap.

list_prometheus_rules returned no data for rule_name RequestErrorRate and for match {severity="warning"}, so the alert expression and the 2.3555 payload value could not be verified, and the alert's current firing/resolved state is not observable with the available tools.
The frontend container log query for 03:25-03:54:48 returned no lines (status no_data), so no frontend application-level error text is available.
The ad container log read returned only one line ('Ad service starting.' at 03:36:01); whether additional startup output exists outside retention is unknown.
Who or what issued the ad restart (annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-15T03:31:48Z) is unknown: the change_history integration is not available in this Run.

Services cart, checkout, currency, email, product-catalog, quote, shipping, kafka, image-provider, load-generator and jaeger-all-in-one returned no error-span series in the error query, which is unknown rather than proven zero; their health was not otherwise verified.

No CPU-throttling or JVM startup metric exists in the queried metric set (a get_metric_names query for rpc_/http_server/app_ names returned no data), so the low 50m CPU limit as the reason for slow ad startup remains an unverified hypothesis.

Exact failed-request counts cannot be stated from these span counters: they are extrapolated and sparse at window edges (whole-window increase gives 424.1 error spans per layer while coarser 5-minute buckets sum lower), so the number of failed /api/data requests is approximately 420, not exact.
Ad serving timeline resolution is coarse: the ad GetAds series was only available in 300s windows, so the precise minute the ad process began serving again between ~03:37 and ~03:42 is unknown.
next_steps: Add and tune a readiness/startup probe for the ad container (TCP or gRPC health on port 8080) and verify the Deployment keeps traffic off until the app is listening.
Raise ad replicas to at least 2 with a PodDisruptionBudget and/or a rollout strategy that cannot remove the only serving replica.
Confirm whether the 03:31:48 rollout restart of ad was planned, correlating with the change record once change history is available.
Check Alertmanager for the current state of RequestErrorRate (frontend error spans stopped after ~03:41) and consider widening the 'above 0' threshold to reduce single-dependency blips.
Evaluate container CPU throttling for the ad pod to see whether the 50m limit is delaying JVM startup.

view.series_note: traces_span_metrics_calls_total counts spans of every operation of the service (internal, client and server spans alike), summed over the labels kept in this query; it is not a count of requests. status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET means the span carried no status; it does not mean the call succeeded.
